title: A reckless gamble using oneself as a chess piece
next_chapter_hook: From the depths of the Cosmic Eye came Cang Yutian's furious voice: 'You are playing with fire!'

text.content: The phantom of the Destiny Writer trembled slightly, those ancient eyes that could see through eternity suddenly narrowing: 'It seems you are more interesting than I anticipated—and more valuable.' These words exploded like thunder in Chen Ji's Mental Sea, yet they did not instill fear. On the contrary, a faint smile curved Chen Ji's lips, a smile socalm yet近乎残忍. 'Value?' He silently念叨这两个字 in his heart, fingertips gently stroking the warm Tianji Record Fragment hidden in his sleeve. 'Do you find a chess piece interesting, or is it that this chess piece has finally decided to move?' He did not speak aloud, but that silent mockery seemed to penetrate the barrier between illusion and reality. A subtle fluctuation crossed those omniscient eyes of the Destiny Writer—was it curiosity, or... wariness? Chen Ji knew, his gamble was correct.

From the depths of his Mental Sea, Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul spoke in a hollow voice, carrying an unusual gravity: 'Boy, you're insane. Exposing yourself directly to the Heavenly Eye's gaze, your fate trajectory will be completely exposed.' Chen Ji did not respond, merely closing his eyes slowly. In the darkness, countless points of light emerged like fireflies in the depths of consciousness—those were the chess pieces he had secretly positioned over the years, each point a hidden thread connecting the corners of the Three Great Sects, the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path, and even the Ancient Forbidden Land. He had spent a full ten years laying this chessboard, all for this moment. 'Mo Xiansheng,' he finally spoke, his voice terrifyingly calm, 'you said the more complete the Tianji Record, the stronger the fatal backlash of fate.' The remnant soul fell silent for a moment, seemingly realizing something. 'But what you didn't say was—' Chen Ji opened his eyes, a wild light burning in his pupils, 'When this fatal backlash rushes toward the chess player, the greatest variable on the chessboard is no longer the piece, but... the Chess Player himself.'

dialogue.content: 'Interesting.' The Destiny Writer's voice was no longer cold as a machine, gaining a hint of evaluative interest. 'Are you telling me that you—atrash who hasn't even formed a Golden Core—intend to threaten me?' A contemptuous arc appeared at the corner of the phantom's lips, the expression of a god gazing down at an ant. 'For hundreds of millions of years, countless prophets, rebels against the Dao, and heaven-defying beings have spoken similar words. Their ashes still drift in the River of Heavenly Dao.' Chen Ji did not retreat, instead taking a step forward. 'Then tell me—' his voice abruptly turned cold, 'among those ashes, was there even one person who made you lose three thousand years of布局 before they died?'

choice.prompt: Facing the Destiny Writer's pressure, Chen Ji needed to make a choice in an instant—how should this reckless gamble begin?

choices.text: All-in: directly detonate the fifth page of the Tianji Record

This move is extremely dangerous, but if successful, it will directly tear open the ultimate chess player's defenses.

choices.visible_reward: Gain the [Tianji Disorder] status, the Destiny Writer's Foresight Ability is temporarily nullified for one hour
choices.risk_hint: Once failed, you will be directly exposed under the full scrutiny of the Heavenly Eye, with no escape

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, his fingers pressing abruptly onto the warm Fragment hidden in his sleeve. In an instant, the fifth page of the Tianji Record seemed to come alive, countless ancient seal characters slithering off the paper surface like poisonous snakes, racing along his meridians straight into his Mental Sea. Agonizing pain flooded in like a tide, blood seeping from his seven orifices, yet his smile grew more brilliant. 'Didn't you want to know what value I have?' His voice was hoarse but carried an iron will, 'Now, you shall soon discover—when a chess piece chooses to self-destruct, even the Chess Player cannot remain uninvolved.' The Tianji Record Fragment trembled violently in his sleeve, a primordial power capable of disrupting Heavenly Dao's operation began to accumulate within Chen Ji's body, awaiting the final release.

For the first time, the phantom of the Destiny Writer showed obvious fluctuation. Those ancient eyes that could see through eternity abruptly contracted, as if witnessing something inconceivable. 'Impossible—the seal on the fifth page, even I cannot fully decipher—' Chen Ji grinned, blood dripping from his chin, making him appear even more savage and mad. 'You overlooked one thing,' his voice was low like a dragon's roar from the abyss, 'the Tianji Record does not choose geniuses or the strong, but a—a lunatic driven to the brink by fate. And what lunatics do best is, in desperate circumstances, blow up the entire mountain.'

choices.text: Slow and steady: activate partial abilities to create a fog of uncertainty
choices.description: Do not fully release the fifth page's power, but instead use the Tianji Record Fragment's instinctive aura to create a fog of fate, gradually interfering with the Destiny Writer's foresight ability, trading time for space.

text.content: Chen Ji did not rush. He slowly closed his eyes, sinking his consciousness into the core of the Tianji Record Fragment. Not forcibly prying open that sealed forbidden power, but in the posture of a guide, gently knocking on that sleeping instinct. The Fragment warmed slightly, emitting wisps of mist-like aura—those were the Tianji Record's instinctive backlash as a Heavenly chess piece, specifically designed to interfere with fate observers' judgment. 'What do you see?' Chen Ji silently念叨 in his heart, a cunning smile appearing at the corner of his lips, 'Are you certain that what you see is what I want you to see?'

For the first time, the Destiny Writer's brow truly furrowed. It discovered that its originally clear vision had begun to show a faint mist; Chen Ji's fate trajectory was no longer a straight line, but like a coiling snake—blurred and difficult to grasp. 'Interesting.' Its voice lowered, gaining a hint of serious evaluation, 'You are using the power I gave you, to interfere with me in return.' Chen Ji slowly opened his eyes, his gazecalm如水. 'You are mistaken,' his voice carried a快意 of mockery, 'you merely thought you gave power. In truth, what you gave was a—chess piece that bites back.'

choices.text: Feint east, strike west: secretly contact external forces for intervention
choices.description: Use the already-buried secret pieces to release signals to the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path or the Ancient Forbidden Land, attracting third-party forces to intervene, forcing the ultimate chess player's attention to be diverted.
choices.visible_cost: Consume 15 points of Heavenly Fate, expose one secret piece that has been dormant for years
choices.visible_reward: The Destiny Writer's attention is diverted, you gain an action window of at least three hours
choices.risk_hint: The introduced external forces may spiral out of control, causing greater variables and dangers
choices.process_label: exchange minimal cost for maximal gain

text.content: Chen Ji's fingers silently formed an ancient hand seal within his sleeve—a secret communication technique passed down between the inheritors of the Tianji Record and the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path. In an instant, a hidden message pierced through layers of void and landed in a distant dark palace. Ye Qing, who had been meditating, suddenly opened her eyes, a flash of astonishment crossing her gaze before transforming into a knowing smile. "Chen Ji, Chen Ji, you've finally come to me." She murmured softly, her fingertips forming a responding seal. At the same time, somewhere deep within the seals of the Ancient Forbidden Land, an existence that had slumbered for ten thousand years opened its eyes at the same moment—the last trump card Chen Ji had planted ten years ago.

The phantom of the Fate Writer tilted its head slightly, as if sensing something. Its gaze pierced through layers of void, seeing the eerie light emanating from the direction of the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path, and perceiving the ancient fluctuation coming from the Ancient Forbidden Land. "Are you calling for reinforcements?" Its voice carried a playful tone, "Interesting, using the pieces that already existed in the chess game I set up to disturb this chess master's line of sight." Chen Ji only smiled faintly, that smile hiding the depth and ruthlessness of a ten-year plan. "You're mistaken," his voice low and confident, "This isn't calling for reinforcements—it's telling you that the true chess masters were never just one."

No matter what method Chen Ji chose to begin, the wheels of fate had already begun to turn. Deep within his Mental Sea, the seal on the fifth page of the Tianji Record showed fine cracks under Chen Ji's probing. A power sufficient to make even the Eyes of Heavenly Way take notice was slowly awakening. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul let out a long sigh: "Boy, you've taken too dangerous a step." Chen Ji did not answer, his consciousness firmly locked onto that wisp of awakening power, feeling its entanglement with his own Heavenly Fate. For fifty years, he had been waiting for this moment—not for revenge, not for power, but to prove one thing: "A piece can also eat the chess master."

dialogue.content: "Eat me?" The Fate Writer's laughter echoed through the void, carrying a pitying arrogance. "Do you know why none of the past inheritors of the Tianji Record could threaten me? Because they were too smart, smart enough to know when to retreat." Its phantom stepped forward, those eyes reflecting Chen Ji's pale face. "And you, a waste who hasn't even formed a Golden Core, on what basis do you think you can succeed?" Chen Ji raised his head, letting blood trickle from the corner of his eye, yet his gaze was clearer than ever. "Because they were smart, so they lost." His voice was terrifyingly calm, "And I'm foolish, so I dare to do what they didn't dare to do—like using my own life to distract you for one second."

text.content: At this moment of extreme tension, an unusual fluctuation suddenly came from deep within Chen Ji's Mental Sea. It was a voice from the depths of the fifth page seal of the Tianji Record—not Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul, but a will imprint left by an even more ancient and majestic existence. "Interesting child." That voice was aged and profound, as if traversing endless years. "Since you've chosen to knock on this door in this manner, I'll give you one chance—" Chen Ji's heart trembled. This was a realm that no previous inheritor of the Tianji Record had ever touched. "Remember, the power of the fifth page is not for attack, but for rewriting. When the Fate Writer examines you, you can also... examine it." These words exploded like thunder in Chen Ji's Mental Sea, and a unprecedented plan quickly took shape in his mind.

choice.prompt: The hidden will of the fifth page of the Tianji Record provided the key hint—rewrite, not attack. Facing this rare opportunity, what should Chen Ji choose as his next move?

choices.text: Use the rewriting power to turn the tables
choices.description: Using the rewriting power of the fifth page of the Tianji Record, forcibly modify one's own fate trajectory under the watchful gaze of the ultimate chess master—not to hide, but to show the Fate Writer a "future" it absolutely wouldn't expect.

choices.visible_reward: The Fate Writer's foresight will have a fatal deviation, granting you at least six hours of strategic advantage
choices.risk_hint: The disturbance of rewriting fate is extremely large, which may expose more trump cards, but could also make the ultimate chess master take you seriously
choices.process_label: dominate and prove you're the true player

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, pouring all his consciousness into the core of the fifth page of the Tianji Record. In an instant, his Mental Sea transformed into a vast sea of stars, with him standing at the very center of this starry sea. "What are you doing?" For the first time, the Fate Writer's voice carried obvious wariness. "Rewriting." Chen Ji's voice was calm as water, yet carried an irresistible authority. He stretched out his hand and traced a fate that had never existed in the void—in that fate, he did not die under Heavenly Way's backlash, but successfully fused all nine pages of the Tianji Record, becoming an existence that transcended the Heavenly Way. "Don't you like watching the future?" Chen Ji grinned, that smile carrying a mad joy, "Then take a good look at this—this is the 'future' you should be most worried about."

The phantom of the Fate Writer trembled violently. Those eyes that had seen through all ages showed a tremor for the first time upon seeing the "future" Chen Ji traced. It saw an image that shouldn't exist—the nine pages of the Tianji Record merging into one, transcending the Heavenly Way, standing above the river of fate. This "future" shouldn't have appeared, because according to its design, the Tianji Record could never be complete. But now, a waste who hadn't even formed a Golden Core was writing this possibility before it. "You—" Its voice cracked for the first time, "How could you—This isn't true! This cannot happen!" Chen Ji put away his smile, his gaze cold as an abyss. "You're wrong," his voice low and lethal, "From the moment I obtained the first page fragment, this 'impossibility' has been growing on your chessboard."

choices.text: Use the rewriting power to examine the ultimate chess master in reverse
choices.description: Instead of changing one's own fate, use the rewriting power of the fifth page to examine the Fate Writer's true appearance in reverse—what is it really? Where are its weaknesses?

choices.visible_reward: Obtain crucial intelligence about the Fate Writer, unlock a hidden ability

text.content: Chen Ji did not rush to rewrite his own fate. Instead, he transformed the rewriting power of the fifth page of the Tianji Record into an invisible blade, quietly piercing toward that lofty phantom. "What are you doing?" The Fate Writer's voice suddenly turned sharp, "A mere mortal, daring to—" Before it finished, Chen Ji saw it. Behind that phantom, was hidden a truth it had never shown to any existence. "So that's how it is." Chen Ji's voice was low, carrying the joy of sudden enlightenment, "You're not the true chess master—you're also just a piece, a piece manipulated by the body of the Heavenly Way. Your arrogance, your control, your loftiness—nothing but a mask hiding fear."

The phantom of the Fate Writer trembled violently. That always-arrogant face showed, for the first time, an expression mingling fear and fury. "You—how could you see these—this is forbidden—this is—" Chen Ji interrupted its incoherence, his voice calm to the point of cruelty. "This is what you're most afraid of me discovering, isn't it?" A cold smile curved his lips, "The so-called ultimate chess master is merely another prisoner in a cage. You control fate, yet cannot control your own fate; you examine all beings, yet dare not be examined by them." He stepped forward, his gaze like a blade, "In the end, you're just like me—a wretched creature trying to climb off this chessboard."

choices.text: Rewrite fate while simultaneously performing reverse examination
choices.description: Divide the power of the fifth page of the Tianji Record in two—one half used to rewrite one's own fate trajectory, the other half used to examine the ultimate chess master in reverse. The greatest risk, but possibly the richest rewards.
choices.visible_cost: Consume 70 points of Heavenly Fate, endure double backlash, may cause damage to divine sense
choices.visible_reward: Simultaneously obtain both benefits of fate rewriting and crucial intelligence, and plant the seeds of fear in the ultimate chess master's heart
choices.risk_hint: Dispersing power may result in neither aspect being perfected; if detected by the opponent, may fall into a passive situation
choices.process_label: go all in, completely overturn the board

text.content: Chen Ji formed seals with both hands, and the power of the fifth page of the Tianji Record exploded within his body. Half transformed into brilliant starlight, sketching out a 'future' that transcended the Heavenly Dao; the other half became a dark current, silently piercing into the core of the Destiny Writer. "You're insane--" For the first time, true fear appeared in the Destiny Writer's voice. "Aren't you afraid of not being able to withstand this dual backlash?" Chen Ji didn't answer, his consciousness on the verge of collapse under the tearing of two forces, yet his gaze was clearer than ever. "Afraid?" He squeezed out the word through gritted teeth, blood from his lips staining his lapels. "I've been afraid for fifty years, afraid to the point where I'm still a nobody. Since being afraid changes nothing, then why not—go completely mad!"

At the edge of consciousness collapse, Chen Ji saw everything he wanted to see. The Destiny Writer's true form, its weaknesses, the real manipulator behind it—all truths flashed before him like a carousel. Simultaneously, he sensed the rewritten destiny quietly taking root within the cracks of heaven's design, like an inescapable seed. "Enough." Chen Ji abruptly withdrew his consciousness, staggering backward as if drained of strength, yet a relieved smile spread across his face. "Now, I understand." His voice was hoarse yet firm. "You're not invincible—you've simply been overly inflated in reputation."

Regardless of Chen Ji's choices, the Destiny Writer's reactions exceeded his expectations. The phantom showed no anger, no attack, not even continued threats—it simply watched Chen Ji quietly, and for the first time, an emotion Chen Ji had never seen appeared in those eyes that scrutinized countless ages. "You remind me of someone." Its voice suddenly became low and distant, as if traversing endless years. "Long ago, there was another insignificant creature like you who spoke similar words before me." Chen Ji's heart tightened, acutely catching the key information in these words. "What happened to that person afterward?" he asked. The Destiny Writer fell silent for a moment, then slowly spoke: "He died. But his death prevented me from sleeping peacefully for the next thirty thousand years."

The words struck like cold water on Chen Ji's head, yet his blood boiled. Thirty thousand years—for an entity that prided itself as the ultimate chess master to be troubled for so long, what had that 'insignificant creature' done? Chen Ji suddenly realized he might be replicating a path no one had ever successfully walked. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul sighed faintly in the depths of his Mental Sea: "Kid, your step... came too fast. So fast that I couldn't even warn you—the real danger isn't whether you can overturn the chessboard, but whether you have the ability to clean up the aftermath." Chen Ji didn't respond. His gaze passed through the Destiny Writer's phantom, looking toward the endless void. There, he seemed to see a blurry figure watching him, its eyes carrying an indescribable sense of anticipation.

dialogue.content: "What is your name?" the Destiny Writer suddenly asked, its tone showing less arrogance and more... seriousness? Chen Ji slightly froze, then reported his name. "Chen Ji." The phantom repeated this name, as if savoring it. "Ji... the Ji of mechanisms, the Ji of opportunities," its voice suddenly became somewhat ethereal, "A good name. This name reminds me of another person—his name is Chen Xuan, the previous inheritor of the Tianji Record." Chen Ji's pupils sharply contracted. Chen Xuan—that was a name he had seen in the fragments of the Tianji Record, also a taboo that Mo Xiansheng had never mentioned directly. "Do you know him?" he asked, trying to keep his voice calm. The Destiny Writer's phantom let out an ambiguous laugh: "Know? No, I know him better than anyone. After all—I personally sent him to his death."

choice.prompt: The Destiny Writer proactively mentioned Chen Xuan—the previous inheritor of the Tianji Record, Chen Ji's ancestor. This information was too shocking, and Chen Ji needed to react in an instant.

choices.visible_reward: Obtaining key intelligence about Chen Xuan and the Tianji Record's inheritance, potentially unlocking hidden plotlines

text.content: Chen Ji drew a deep breath, suppressing the turbulent emotions raging within. "What did Chen Xuan do?" He stared directly into those all-knowing eyes, his voice steady yet carrying an irrepressible urgency. "For you to personally intervene, it must have been no small matter." The Destiny Writer's phantom rippled slightly, as if lost in memory. "He discovered my secret." Its voice dropped low. "Just like what you did—examining me in reverse, seeing things that should never be seen." Chen Ji's heart shook. "But he was more radical than you," the phantom's tone carried a complex emotion. "He not only wanted to overturn the chessboard, he wanted to—destroy the entire Heavenly Dao."

Chen Ji froze. Destroy the Heavenly Dao? Chen Xuan—his ancestor, the man recorded in the Tianji Record as having merely 'accidentally fallen'—had actually harbored such a crazy plan? "He failed," the Destiny Writer continued, its tone carrying an indefinable emotion. "But his failure wasn't because of me—it was because he discovered another truth." Chen Ji lifted his head sharply: "What truth?" The phantom fell silent for a moment, then slowly uttered four words: "His daughter." Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. A thought flashed through his mind—Chen Nian, his missing sister, the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key' taken away by the Holy Sect—what connection did she have with Chen Xuan?

text.content: Chen Ji didn't ask further. He simply stood there quietly, a faint smile appearing on his face—calm to the point of coldness. "What do you want to tell me?" he asked back, his tone carrying a hint of mockery. "Chen Xuan's affairs, I'll find the answers myself. As for you—" He paused, his gaze sharp as a blade. "Why are you proactively telling me these things?" The Destiny Writer's phantom clearly froze. It clearly hadn't expected Chen Ji to be so composed, not追问 or getting agitated as it had anticipated. "Don't you care about your ancestor?" its voice carried a probing tone. "I do care." Chen Ji nodded. "But I care more about—why you want me to care."

Silence spread through the void. The Destiny Writer's phantom stared at Chen Ji, those all-knowing eyes flickering with complex light. "Interesting." It finally spoke, its tone carrying genuine respect. "You have more composure than your ancestor." Chen Ji remained unmoved, simply saying: "He lost because he was too impatient. I won't repeat his mistakes." The phantom suddenly laughed, the laughter echoing through the void, carrying an ambiguous meaning of either appreciation or mockery. "Good, very good." Its voice suddenly became profound. "Since you're so composed, I'll give you a gift—your sister Chen Nian, she's still alive." Chen Ji's gaze finally flickered, but he quickly suppressed it. "I know." His voice was calm as still water. "This is a situation I orchestrated for ten years."

choices.text: Pretend to inquire about Chen Xuan, but actually probe the Holy Sect
choices.description: On the surface appearing very interested in Chen Xuan's affairs, but actually wanting to take this opportunity to gather intelligence about the relationship between the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path and the Destiny Writer—Ye Qing mentioned that the Holy Sect has been using her all along, but is there an invisible hand manipulating things behind the scenes?

choices.visible_reward: Obtaining hidden intelligence about the relationship between the Holy Sect and the Heavenly Dao under the opponent's unguarded state

text.content: Chen Ji pretended to ponder, a hint of worry appearing between his brows. "Chen Xuan... I've only seen his name in fragments of the Tianji Record Fragment." His voice slowed, as if struggling to recall something. "They say he left behind a complete scheme, but the specifics..." He shifted the topic, his gaze casually sweeping across the depths of the Void. "By the way, I've always been curious—what is the Holy Sect's relationship with you?" The phantom of the Fate Chronicler visibly froze. Obviously, Chen Ji's question caught it off guard. "Why do you ask this?" Its tone turned wary. Chen Ji shrugged, wearing an innocent expression: "Just curious. After all, the Holy Sect has been searching for the Tianji Record Fragment all this time. I assumed..." He didn't finish, but the pause was perfectly placed.

The Fate Chronicler fell silent for a moment, then let out a meaningful chuckle. "You're probing me." There was no anger in its tone, instead gaining a hint of playfulness. "Good, very good. You used Chen Xuan as bait, but actually wanted to know the relationship between the Holy Sect and Heavenly Secrets—you're more cunning than I anticipated." Chen Ji offered a noncommittal smile. "Since you've seen through it, I won't pretend anymore." His gaze turned sharp. "What does the Holy Sect want with the Tianji Record? Who is their true master behind the scenes?" The phantom's lips curved into a sardonic arc: "You really want to know?" Chen Ji nodded. "Fine." The Fate Chronicler's voice suddenly turned ice-cold. "Behind the Holy Sect is me. Or rather—part of me."

The answer struck like a thunderclap in Chen Ji's mind. The Holy Sect's master was the Eye of Heavenly Secrets—in other words, the Holy Sect's millennia-long pursuit of the Tianji Record Fragment was merely a play directed by the Fate Chronicler? Chen Ji suddenly thought of Ye Qing—that woman who had been controlled and exploited by the Holy Sect her entire life. She thought she was rebelling against fate, unaware that every act of her rebellion was scripted within destiny's grand play. "You told her the Holy Sect was her shackle," Chen Ji's voice was low, "but the true shackle is actually you." The Fate Chronicler didn't deny it, merely saying coolly: "Chess pieces don't need to understand the full picture of the chessboard." Chen Ji clenched his fists, his fingernails digging deep into his palms. "What if—" he spoke each word deliberately, "the chess piece wants not just to overturn the board, but to drag the Chess Player down into the abyss?"

The phantom of the Fate Chronicler froze completely at that moment. Those eyes that had seen through eons stared intently at Chen Ji, as if seeing this ant-like creature truly for the first time. "Are you threatening me?" Its voice held no arrogance, only an indescribable complexity. "Not a threat." Chen Ji shook his head. "A notice." He took a step forward, and his entire aura underwent a subtle transformation at that moment—no longer a submissivetrash, but a madman erupting from the depths of desperation. "You just said Chen Xuan's rebellion kept you from sleeping for thirty thousand years." A cruel smile curved his lips. "So what if I told you my goal isn't to rob you of sleep—but to make you disappear completely?" Within the depths of his Mental Sea, the seal on the fifth page of the Tianji Record cracked open at that moment, a force sufficient to change heaven and earth slowly awakening.

dialogue.content: Silence. Endless silence. When the Fate Chronicler spoke again, its voice carried an emotion Chen Ji had never heard before—not fear, not anger, but a sigh almost akin to appreciation. "Chen Ji." It was the first time it solemnly pronounced this name. "Do you know, among the 137 Tianji Record inheritors of the past, only two have made me think 'this person might actually succeed'?" Chen Ji said nothing, merely watching it quietly. "The first was Chen Xuan—he almost succeeded." The phantom's voice lowered. "And the second—is you." Chen Ji bared his teeth in a grin, blood seeping from between his teeth, making him appear even more ferocious. "Then you'd better memorize this face clearly." His voice was hoarse yet firm. "Because the days to come, you'll have to live under the shadow of this person—just like your 137 predecessors."
